subject.title: macOS update can leave manual-update loop and stale node host causing Gateway restart storm

question: Should this canonical macOS manual updater-loop report be resolved as one core lifecycle fix, split into narrower launchd/no-op/node-skew trackers, or closed only after live current-main macOS proof shows the full loop is gone?
rationale: The current evidence shows multiple partially fixed surfaces, but the permanent behavior involves maintainer-owned update contract and recovery UX choices rather than one clearly safe code edit.

options.title: Keep Canonical And Define Contract
options.body: Use this issue as the canonical manual updater-loop tracker while maintainers choose the update/no-op/dedupe and recovery UX contract before implementation.

options.title: Split Narrow Trackers
options.body: Move stale-job detection, duplicate update prevention, launchd bootstrap recovery, and node-host restart guidance into separate canonical issues if owners want smaller proof lanes.

options.title: Close After Live Proof
options.body: Close only if a real current-main or latest-release macOS LaunchAgent update smoke proves no stale jobs, no Gateway loop, and no stale node-host recovery gap.

recommendation.title: Keep Canonical And Define Contract
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the canonical manual updater-loop tracker while maintainers choose the update/no-op/dedupe and recovery UX contract before implementation.
